title: Desk Guidance Note: Refund Credits on Deficiency Balance Accounts
content:
**Rule.** A credit is applied only to an account held under Deficiency Balance Accounts whose status is open, on payment plan or on settlement plan, as the account record shows. Only refunds on the cashiering card's list are credited: unearned CPI premium, GAP waiver and service-contract refunds issued after the contract was liquidated, and recovery expenses later found charged in error; each credit is linked to its originating record and applied once. A credit reduces the balance on its posting date; during an installment settlement it also reduces the remaining settlement amount, and a credit larger than the balance is limited to the balance, the issuing product paying any excess to the borrower.

## Condition, judgement, result

| Condition | Judgement | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Account status open, on payment plan or on settlement plan | Status allows a credit | The credit may be applied |
| Any other status | Status does not allow a credit | No credit is applied |
| Refund is one of the listed kinds | Source accepted | Credited, linked to its originating record, once |
| Credit larger than the balance | Limited | Credited up to the balance; the issuing product pays the excess to the borrower |
| Account on settlement plan | Settlement in progress | The credit also reduces the remaining settlement amount |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A GAP waiver refund of $400.00 reaches an open account whose balance is $1,500.00. The balance falls to $1,100.00 on the posting date.
- A service-contract refund of $900.00 reaches an open account whose balance is $600.00. $600.00 is credited and the balance reaches zero; the remaining $300.00 is paid to the borrower by the issuing product.
- The same originating refund record never produces a second credit.
